concern.concern: Proof 2.1 chooses a disk 'of least transverse width modulo the deck translations' without defining that width or establishing attainment, then asserts that intersections with translates produce a smaller-width disk. This is the thin part of the argument that a planar bigon projects injectively to the torus. The standard bigon criterion supplies the intended justification, but the stated minimization needs clarification or an exact external-input citation.

original_verdict.reason: The Bézout construction gives an essential simple representative, intersection with a dual curve proves primitivity, and the annular-cover bigon argument reduces equal primitive classes to disjoint parallel curves, hence isotopy.

concern.concern: Proof 1.1 says the face maps are hyperbolic isometries 'because their three corresponding ideal vertices have the same cross-ratio shape.' A triple has no cross-ratio shape, and adjacent tetrahedra need not have equal shapes. The justification is that any bijection between the vertices of two ideal triangular faces extends to their hyperbolic face isometry.
